title: Emissions and cost tradeoffs of time-matched clean electricity procurement under inter-annual weather variability -- case study of hydrogen production
summary: Regulators and voluntary corporate sustainability efforts are increasingly adopting time-matching requirements (TMRs) for clean electricity procurement for large loads, such as data centers, and electricity-intensive fuel production, such as hydrogen. We use a stochastic capacity expansion model (CEM) framework to assess how inter-annual weather variability affects the cost, composition, and emissions of procurement-driven infrastructure to meet annual and hourly TMRs using the case study of a grid-connected hydrogen producer in Texas.
